prompt:
A single compound was assayed by IC50 against a single protein target in two different assays, reported in the literature.

Compound SMILES: CNCCC(Oc1ccc(C(F)(F)F)cc1)c1ccccc1
Target (ChEMBL): CHEMBL228

Assay A:
  Description: Displacement of [I125]RTI-55 from human SERT transfected in human HEK293 cells
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Homo sapiens
  Cell type: HEK293

Assay B:
  Description: Inhibition of human SERT expressed in HEK293 cells at incubated for 15 mins by neurotransmitter reuptake assay
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Homo sapiens
  Cell type: HEK293

Will the two reported IC50 values agree closely (within 0.3 log units), or differ substantially (more than 1.0 log units)?

Respond with exactly this JSON and nothing else:
{"call": "COMMENSURABLE" | "NOT_COMMENSURABLE" | "INSUFFICIENT_INFO",
 "confidence": <float 0-1>,
 "error_class": "assay_method" | "buffer_conditions" | "construct_mutant" | "organism" | "readout_type" | "potency_range" | "none" | "other",
 "reason": "<one sentence>"}

"COMMENSURABLE" means you expect the two reported values to agree closely.
"NOT_COMMENSURABLE" means you expect them to differ substantially.
error_class is your primary reason for a NOT_COMMENSURABLE call, else "none".
raw: {"call": "NOT_COMMENSURABLE", "confidence": 0.62, "error_class": "assay_method", "reason": "Assay A is a radioligand binding displacement assay measuring affinity at the transporter, while Assay B is a functional neurotransmitter reuptake inhibition assay; these different methodologies (binding vs. uptake) frequently yield IC50 values that differ by more than 1.0 log unit for serotonin transporter ligands."}
